note: Map anchors for the historical-event archive (src/data/historicalEvents.json, corrected v1.1 records). kind=point: a verified coordinate, source cited in anchorNote. kind=region: the record is region-level; the marker sits at the region's official IAU/USGS Gazetteer center for orientation and is NOT an event position. No anchor is invented: events without a verified coordinate get no point marker anywhere.

markers.anchorNote: Marker = the InSight lander (existing verified mission-site position), the DETECTION site of both seismic records - NOT the epicenters. The 2022 quake's epicenter was later placed close to but outside the Cerberus Fossae region, over 2000 km away; the 2019 record's source does not fix an epicenter.

The impact crater itself, located by MRO before/after imaging at 35.1 N, 189.82 E (Posiolova et al., Science 2022, as restated in doi.org/10.1029/2024JE008875). Seismic detection was by InSight, thousands of km away.
Coordinates from the HiRISE observation metadata (~83.7 N, 235.8 E, cited in the event record).

Marker = Jezero crater center (IAU/USGS Gazetteer, 47.5 km crater) for orientation only. These four records are crater-level context: no exact event positions are pinned. The Sol 215 record happened at the rover; the Sol 899 / Sol 1398 dust devils were imaged kilometers AWAY from the rover (not at it); the Jan 2022 storm was regional.

Marker = Gale crater center (IAU/USGS Gazetteer, 154 km crater) for orientation only. Both records are crater-level context: the 2018 event was planet-encircling (observed in-situ by Curiosity) and the Sol 1597 dust devil was seen at a distance from the rover - no exact positions pinned.
